subtitle: In Vallabhi’s quiet halls, a philosopher turns debate into a living refuge for the mind.

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle wide of Vallabhi’s monastery complex against a hazy Saurashtra sky
panels.action: Sthiramati stands at the edge of a stone terrace in Vallabhi, robes stirring in the coastal wind, gazing over courtyards filled with monks and palm-leaf manuscripts.

dialogue.text: In Maitraka Vallabhi, where kings minted copper and stories of power, Sthiramati built something stranger and stronger: a monastery made not of stone, but of thought.

i18n.hi: म Maitraka वल्लभी में, जहाँ राजा तांबे और सत्ता की कथाएँ गढ़ते थे, स्थिरमती ने कुछ और अजीब और मज़बूत बनाया: पत्थर नहीं, विचारों से बना विहार।

panels.shot: slow push-in from cityscape to monastery cluster inside Vallabhi
panels.action: The bustling streets of Vallabhi give way to the calmer inner quarter, where tiled roofs of monasteries rise amid mango trees and quiet cloisters.

dialogue.text: The Maitrakas ruled Vallabhi in the sixth century, carving a capital of copper trade and royal grants. Yet behind the markets, monks turned this western city into a seat of Buddhist learning.

i18n.hi: छठी सदी में मैत्रकों ने वल्लभी पर राज किया, तांबे के व्यापार और राजकीय दान से राजधानी गढ़ी। पर बाज़ारों के पीछे, भिक्षु इस पश्चिमी नगर को बौद्ध विद्या का केंद्र बना रहे थे।

panels.shot: medium interior shot of a simple lecture hall
panels.action: Inside a long hall, young monks sit cross-legged around low desks; at the far end, Sthiramati, calm and intent, leans over a palm-leaf manuscript, stylus poised.

dialogue.text: Tradition places Sthiramati here, among Vallabhi’s cloisters, as a student of Gunamati and a sharp voice in Yogacara thought. The records name his works more clearly than his life.

i18n.hi: परंपरा स्थिरमती को यहीं, वल्लभी के विहारों में रखती है—गुणमती का शिष्य, और योगाचार विचार में तेज़ स्वर। अभिलेख उसकी रचनाओं को उसके जीवन से ज़्यादा साफ़ नाम लेते हैं।

panels.shot: close-up on a palm-leaf manuscript being unrolled
panels.action: A hand carefully unrolls a palm-leaf bearing fine Sanskrit script; in the margin, small annotation marks cluster beside a section titled "Trimsika".

dialogue.text: In Vallabhi, Sthiramati takes up Vasubandhu’s Trimsika, the Thirty Verses on Consciousness. His Trimsika-vijnaptibhasya bends over each line, asking what it means for mind to shape world.

i18n.hi: वल्लभी में स्थिरमती वसुबन्धु की त्रिंशिका, चेतना पर तीस श्लोक उठाते हैं। उसकी त्रिंशिका-विज्ञप्तिभाष्य हर लाइन पर झुककर पूछती है: जब मन जगत को रचता है, तो इसका मतलब क्या है?

panels.shot: extreme close-up on Sthiramati’s focused eyes in lamplight
panels.action: By an oil lamp, Sthiramati’s eyes narrow in concentration as he reads; shadows of stacked manuscripts surround him like silent companions.

dialogue.text: Yogacara teachings speak of consciousness-only, of seeds, perceptions and illusions. Sthiramati does not only repeat them; he arranges, clarifies, and threads them through Abhidharma analysis.

i18n.hi: योगाचार की शिक्षा केवल-विज्ञान, बीजों, धारणाओं और भ्रांतियों की बात करती है। स्थिरमती इन्हें बस दोहराते नहीं; वे इन्हें सजाते, स्पष्ट करते, और अभिधर्म की सूक्ष्म जाँच में पिरोते हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot of Sthiramati teaching in front of a small gathering
panels.action: Sthiramati sits on a simple raised seat, a board with leaves before him, while a ring of monks listen; his hand sketches a diagram of layered consciousness in the dust.

dialogue.text: First see how perception rises and falls. Only then ask if anything stands behind it.

i18n.hi: पहले देखो, अनुभव कैसे उठता और गिरता है। फिर पूछो, उसके पीछे सच में कुछ खड़ा भी है या नहीं।

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder shot of Sthiramati writing commentary
panels.action: Seen from behind, Sthiramati bends over a fresh leaf, inscribing neat Sanskrit lines; above him, wooden rafters and hanging cloth shields him from the sun’s glare.

dialogue.text: His commentaries do what living speech cannot. They fix arguments into carefully ordered prose, turning the oral flow of debate into a road others can walk again and again.

i18n.hi: उसकी टीकाएँ वह कर पाती हैं जो ज़िंदा वाणी नहीं कर पाती। वे तर्कों को सधी हुई गद्य में जड़ देती हैं, बहस की मौखिक धारा को ऐसी राह बना देती हैं जिसे और लोग बार-बार चल सकें।

panels.shot: wide shot of the monastery courtyard with construction and planting
panels.action: In the courtyard, workers raise a new colonnade while monks plant saplings; Sthiramati stands with a donor, gesturing toward the emerging structure.

dialogue.text: Inscriptions from this age speak of a monk named Sthiramati linked to a Vallabhi monastery. They hint at buildings and endowments, but keep their silence about where he came from, or how he died.

i18n.hi: इस समय के शिलालेख वल्लभी के एक विहार से जुड़े स्थिरमती नाम भिक्षु का ज़िक्र करते हैं। वे इमारतों और दान का इशारा करते हैं, पर उसके जन्म और मृत्यु पर चुप रहते हैं।

panels.shot: split composition: Vallabhi classroom on one side, distant Nalanda towers on the other
panels.action: On one side, Sthiramati addresses students in Vallabhi; on the other, faintly imagined, the towering brick structures of Nalanda rise under the eastern sky.

dialogue.text: Far to the east, Nalanda’s Dharmapala also shapes Yogacara. Later Chinese translators will set Sthiramati’s Vallabhi line and Dharmapala’s Nalanda line side by side, tracing their subtle disagreements.

i18n.hi: पूर्व में नालंदा के धर्मपाल भी योगाचार को आकार दे रहे हैं। बाद के चीनी अनुवादक स्थिरमती की वल्लभी परम्परा को धर्मपाल की नालंदा परम्परा के साथ रखकर, उनके महीन मतभेदों का पीछा करेंगे।

panels.shot: medium shot of a debate circle in Vallabhi
panels.action: In a shaded cloister, Sthiramati and another monk sit opposite each other, with students around them; their hands rest calmly on their knees as they speak in turn.

dialogue.text: If consciousness alone is real, tell me: what is this debate that rises between us?

i18n.hi: यदि केवल चेतना ही सच है, तो बताो: हमारे बीच उठती यह बहस क्या है?

panels.shot: close-up of a young monk’s thoughtful face, Sthiramati blurred in the background
panels.action: A young monk furrows his brow, absorbing the exchange; behind him, Sthiramati’s figure is softly out of focus, still speaking with measured clarity.

dialogue.text: For Vallabhi, these arguments are not sport. They are training: to see how craving, ignorance and habit load each moment of awareness, and how careful attention might slowly loosen their grip.

i18n.hi: वल्लभी के लिए ये तर्क खेल नहीं। यह साधना है—देखने की कि कैसे तृष्णा, अविद्या और आदत हर जागरूक क्षण पर बोझ डालते हैं, और कैसे सजग ध्यान धीरे-धीरे उनकी पकड़ ढीली कर सकता है।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye view of scribes copying manuscripts in a hall
panels.action: From above, rows of monks sit in disciplined lines, each copying a text from an exemplar; at the front, Sthiramati oversees, occasionally checking their work.

dialogue.text: As his commentaries spread, copying itself becomes a communal practice. Vallabhi’s halls grow thick with leaves on Yogacara and Abhidharma, anchoring this western city inside wider Buddhist networks.

i18n.hi: जैसे उसकी टीकाएँ फैलती हैं, नकल करना खुद सामूहिक साधना बन जाता है। वल्लभी के प्रांगण योगाचार और अभिधर्म पर पन्नों से भर जाते हैं, इस पश्चिमी नगर को दूर-दूर के बौद्ध जालों से जोड़ते हैं।

panels.shot: imagined montage of scrolls traveling across landscapes
panels.action: A small bundle of manuscripts is carried by a monk along a dusty road, then loaded on a boat, then received in a foreign hall, each scene fading into the next.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, Chinese scholars will translate Yogacara texts and debates shaped by Sthiramati. Vallabhi’s discussions echo in distant languages, even when the city’s own towers fall silent.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद, चीनी विद्वान स्थिरमती से गढ़े योगाचार ग्रंथों और वाद-विवादों का अनुवाद करेंगे। वल्लभी की चर्चाएँ दूर की भाषाओं में गूँजती रहेंगी, जब नगर के खुद के मीनारें खामोश हो जाएँगी।

panels.shot: medium shot of Sthiramati pausing, stylus lifted mid-air
panels.action: Sthiramati sits alone near an open doorway at dusk, palm-leaves in front of him; his stylus hangs paused above the surface as he looks out at the darkening sky.

dialogue.text: Buildings crumble. Will these words hold a path long after our voices fade?

i18n.hi: इमारतें ढहती हैं। क्या ये शब्द हमारी आवाज़ें मिटने के बाद भी राह को थामे रहेंगे?

panels.shot: slow push-in on stacked manuscripts bearing his attributed name
panels.action: A neat stack of palm-leaf texts sits on a wooden shelf, some bearing colophons that name Sthiramati; dust motes drift in a thin shaft of light.

dialogue.text: Modern scholars warn that not every work bearing his name belongs to one man. Identities blur over time, but the style of careful, analytic Yogacara remains, tied to Vallabhi’s memory.

i18n.hi: आज के विद्वान चेताते हैं कि उसके नाम पर चलने वाली हर रचना ज़रूरी नहीं एक ही व्यक्ति की हो। पहचानें धुंधला जाती हैं, पर सजग, विश्लेषी योगाचार की शैली बच रहती है, वल्लभी की याद से बँधी हुई।

panels.shot: wide shot of an empty Vallabhi ruin overlaid with faint figures of monks
panels.action: Stone ruins and scattered foundations lie under the Saurashtra sun; faint, translucent figures of monks at study seem to hover where halls once stood.

dialogue.text: The Maitraka kingdom will pass, and Vallabhi’s walls will fall. Yet inscriptions, manuscripts and far-off translations keep recalling a monastery and a thinker woven into its life.

i18n.hi: मैत्रक राज्य जाएगा, वल्लभी की दीवारें गिरेंगी। पर अभिलेख, पांडुलिपियाँ और दूर के अनुवाद बार-बार एक विहार और उस से गुंथे विचारक को याद करते रहेंगे।

panels.shot: extreme close-up of a modern scholar’s hand turning a page of Levi’s edition
panels.action: In a modern study, a hand turns the pages of Sylvain Levi’s printed Sanskrit edition of Trimsika-vijnaptibhasya; the name 'Sthiramati' appears in bold Roman script.

dialogue.text: When present-day readers open Levi’s edition of Trimsika-vijnaptibhasya, they enter a chain that runs back to Vallabhi. Each note and gloss is a remnant of teaching shaped for real students.

i18n.hi: जब आज का पाठक लेवी की त्रिंशिका-विज्ञप्तिभाष्य खोलता है, वह एक शृंखला में प्रवेश करता है जो वल्लभी तक जाती है। हर टिपण्णी और व्याख्या वास्तविक शिष्यों के लिए गढ़ी शिक्षा का अवशेष है।

panels.shot: medium shot of Sthiramati addressing a circle of monks in twilight
panels.action: In the fading light, Sthiramati speaks to a small circle of monks in the courtyard; the sky is streaked with orange, and the monastery buildings rise quietly around them.

dialogue.text: Do not only argue about mind. Live so that your practice proves your view.

i18n.hi: सिर्फ मन पर बहस मत करो। ऐसे जियो कि तुम्हारी साधना ही तुम्हारे दर्शन को साबित करे।

panels.shot: final wide shot of the monastery dissolving into an abstract pattern of interlinked minds
panels.action: The solid image of the Vallabhi monastery slowly dissolves into an abstract web of silhouettes in contemplation, their outlines linked by faint lines of light.

dialogue.text: Sthiramati’s legacy lies not in a hero’s story, but in a habit: turning sharp thought into shared practice, so a monastery of the mind can outlast stone, kings and names.

i18n.hi: स्थिरमती की विरासत किसी वीर-गाथा में नहीं, एक आदत में है: तीखी सोच को साझा अभ्यास में बदल देना, ताकि मन का विहार पत्थर, राजाओं और नामों से ज़्यादा देर टिक सके।

title_i18n.en: Sthiramati Builds a Monastery of the Mind

subtitle_i18n.en: In Vallabhi’s quiet halls, a philosopher turns debate into a living refuge for the mind.
subtitle_i18n.hi: वल्लभी की शांत दीवारों में, एक दार्शनिक बहस को मन के जिंदा आश्रय में बदल देता है।
